narration.full_text: Namaste students! Welcome to our quiz section on Control and Coordination. We've covered a lot about how organisms respond to their environment. Now, let's test your understanding with some challenging questions. Are you ready? Let's begin! First question: How do auxins promote the growth of a tendril around a support? Describe in brief. Think about how auxins affect cell elongation. The answer is: Auxins produced in the shoot tip move downwards. These auxins cause cell elongation. In tendrils, auxins move away from the contact point with the support. This leads to more growth on the side away from the support, causing the tendril to coil. Next question: Illustrate with the help of a diagram, the effect of auxins in different parts of a plant. This question requires you to visualize the role of auxin. The answer is: Auxin is formed in the apical meristem of the root and shoot. In the shoot, it promotes cell enlargement and inhibits lateral bud development. In the root, it promotes cell division. Moving on to the third question: List in tabular form three differences in the movement of leaves of a Touch-me-not plant when touched and movement of a tendril towards a support. Consider the nature of growth and direction. Here's the answer: Mimosa leaves show growth-independent, fast, and non-directional movement. Tendrils show growth-dependent, slow, and directional movement. And for our final question: (a) Write the names and one function of each of any three growth hormones in plants. (b) In the absence of muscle cells, how do plant cells show movement? Take a moment to recall the plant hormones and their roles. The answer to (a) is: Auxin promotes cell elongation and division. Gibberellins help in stem growth. Cytokinins promote cell division and delay leaf ageing. For (b): Plants use electrical and chemical means to convey information. For instance, Mimosa pudica leaves fold due to turgor pressure changes, which is a growth-independent movement. Great job, everyone! I hope you found this quiz insightful and it helped solidify your understanding of control and coordination.

visual_beats.description: Quiz title: Test Your Knowledge: Control and Coordination
Question: How do auxins promote the growth of a tendril around a support? Describe in brief.

Answer: Auxins produced in the shoot tip move downwards in the plant. These auxins cause cell elongation in the growing tissues. In the tendrils, auxins move away from the point of contact with the supporting object. More growth occurs on the side away from the support. As a result of unequal growth on the two sides, the tendril coils around the support.
Question: Illustrate with the help of a diagram, the effect of auxins in different parts of a plant.

Answer: Diagram illustrating the role of auxin in plant growth. Auxin is formed in the apical meristem of the root and shoot. In the shoot, auxin promotes cell enlargement and inhibits the development of lateral buds. In the root, auxin promotes cell division.
Question: List in tabular form three differences in the movement of leaves of a Touch-me-not plant (the plant of Mimosa family) when touched and movement of a tendril towards a support.
Answer: Mimosa Leaves: Growth independent response, fast process, non-directional. Tendril: Growth dependent response, slow process, directional.
Question: (a) Write the names and one function of each of any three growth hormones in plants. (b) In the absence of muscle cells, how do plant cells show movement?

Answer (a): Auxin: promotes elongation and division. Gibberellins: help in stem growth. Cytokinins: promote cell division and delay leaf ageing. Answer (b): Plants use electrical and chemical means. Mimosa pudica leaves fold due to turgor pressure changes.

verbatim_content.question:
(a) Write the names and one function of each of any three growth hormones in plants.
(b) In the absence of muscle cells, how do plant cells show movement?

(a) Write the names and one function of each of any three growth hormones in plants.
(b) In the absence of muscle cells, how do plant cells show movement?
verbatim_content.answer:
(a) Three growth hormones in plants are-
(i) Auxin: It is synthesized in the young tip of roots and shoots. It promotes elongation and division of cell and root formation.
(ii) Gibberellins: They help in the growth of the stem.
(iii) Cytokinins: They promote cell division and delay leaf ageing.
(b) The ability of a plant to detect change and respond to that change is termed as the sensitivity of the plant. Yet plants have no nervous system and no muscle tissue, they use electrical and chemical means to convey the information from one cell to another cell. The leaves of the sensitive plant (Mimosa pudica) folds up in response to touch. These leaf movements are independent of growth whereas, the directional movement of the shoot of a germinating seedling breaking through the soil is growth dependent.
